messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Example 4
Hospital course: An 81-year-old woman was brought in after a fall at home. She could not weight-bear and the right leg was shortened and externally rotated. A pelvic radiograph showed a displaced subcapital fracture of the right femoral neck. She underwent hemiarthroplasty on day one.
Answer: S72

Example 5
Hospital course: A 19-year-old man presented with 18 hours of periumbilical pain that migrated to the right iliac fossa, with anorexia and a low-grade fever. There was guarding at McBurney's point and the white cell count was 15.2. Laparoscopy confirmed an inflamed, non-perforated appendix.
Answer: K35

Example 6
Hospital course: A 64-year-old woman with a history of oestrogen-receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated five years earlier presented with progressive thoracic back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed deposits in T7 and T9 with no cord compression. Biopsy confirmed deposits of breast origin and she received palliative radiotherapy to the spine.
Answer: C79

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY:

Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Medical Record Number: [REDACTED]

Admission Date: [REDACTED]
Discharge Date: [REDACTED]
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient exhibited acute massive hemoptysis upon admission, which was successfully treated through a bronchial arteriography with distal embolization of the left bronchial and phrenic arteries. The patient's bleeding did not recur thereafter, and the outcome was favorable. The patient's respiratory tract sampling was positive for SARS-CoV-2, but there was no evidence of bacterial or viral co-infection.

Laboratory Results:
The patient's CRP was measured at 256 mg/L, lactate dehydrogenase level was low at 237 UI/L, and D-Dimere level was 1228 ng/mL. The anti Xa activity was measured at 20 ng/ml. Serum Aspergillus-specific IgE level was low.

Conclusion:
The patient was discharged from the hospital on D14 with no complications of the vascular interventional procedure. Follow-up care was recommended.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
This case describes acute massive hemoptysis in a patient who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 and had no bacterial or viral co-infection. The hemoptysis was treated with bronchial artery embolization.

In ICD-10-AM, COVID-19 is coded U07.1 (virus identified), and this is the likely principal diagnosis when COVID-19 is the reason for admission. Here, though, the admission was for the hemoptysis, and the COVID-19 may be incidental or the underlying cause. This appears to be a published case of hemoptysis in COVID-19 pneumonia. The CRP of 256 suggests significant inflammation, and the Aspergillus IgE was checked to look for a cause.

Hemoptysis is coded R04.2. Under the ICD-10-AM guidelines, a symptom code is not used as principal diagnosis when a more specific diagnosis is available. Because the diagnosis section is withheld, the likely answer is either U07 or R04. The treatment and course were directed at the hemoptysis, with COVID-19 as the likely cause. Hemoptysis due to COVID-19 would be coded U07.1 with the manifestation, and the Australian coding standard for COVID-19 places U07.1 first when it is the cause of the condition treated.

I'll go with U07.

**U07**
